title: Neurological deterioration after head injury or cranial surgery
logic: Drop in GCS of 2 or more points, new pupil asymmetry or dilatation, new lateralising weakness, or seizure in a patient with head injury or recent cranial surgery
action: Critical alert: senior review immediately, secure airway if GCS 8 or less, osmotherapy per protocol on anaesthetic advice, emergency imaging or (where none) emergency transfer/exploratory burr hole pathway; record exact times — the interval defines salvageability

title: Cauda equina red flags in back pain
logic: Back pain or sciatica AND any of: bilateral leg pain/weakness, saddle anaesthesia, new urinary retention or incontinence, faecal incontinence, reduced anal tone
action: Emergency referral to spine-capable centre the same day; examine and DOCUMENT perianal sensation, anal tone and post-void residual; do not book physiotherapy or routine imaging — this bypasses the normal queue

title: Shunt blockage or infection
logic: Patient with a CSF shunt presenting with vomiting, drowsiness, irritability, bulging fontanelle, fever without source, headache, or redness/swelling along the shunt tract
action: Same-day referral to the shunt centre — shunt failure kills; do not treat as gastroenteritis or malaria without shunt review; record valve type/setting if known and last revision date

title: GCS severity banding and airway trigger
logic: Head injury encounter with GCS recorded: 13-15 mild, 9-12 moderate, 8 or less severe
action: Auto-band severity on the record; GCS 8 or less raises an airway-protection task and mandates escalation to a centre with airway and imaging capability; moderate band schedules repeat GCS within 30 minutes

title: Serial GCS with timestamps for head injury
logic: Head-injury admission or transfer AND fewer than two timestamped GCS values (with pupil sizes) on the record
action: Block the transfer/operative document until at least two timed GCS-and-pupil observations are captured; the TREND, not a single value, is the surgical trigger

title: Coagulation and anticoagulant check before cranial surgery
logic: Burr hole or craniotomy booked (non-crash) AND no anticoagulant/antiplatelet history recorded or no coagulation correction plan for a patient known to be anticoagulated
action: Prompt for anticoagulant history and reversal/correction plan before listing; for the crash case, flag to the anaesthetic team to run reversal in parallel, never as a reason to delay evacuation of a surgical clot

title: Antibiotic prophylaxis and asepsis bundle for shunt surgery
logic: CSF shunt insertion or revision operative record completed AND prophylactic antibiotic at induction not documented
action: Prompt documentation of the peri-operative antibiotic and the unit implant-asepsis bundle (minimal handling, shunt opened last); shunt infection is the complication that destroys outcomes and the bundle is the defence

title: Open cranial wound bundle — antibiotics and tetanus
logic: Compound skull fracture or penetrating head wound recorded AND (no IV antibiotic time OR tetanus status missing)
action: Block record completion until first-antibiotic time and tetanus prophylaxis are captured; surface elapsed time from arrival if antibiotics not yet given

title: Post-cranial-surgery neuro-observation schedule
logic: Craniotomy, burr hole or shunt procedure completed within the past 24 hours
action: Schedule neuro-observations (GCS, pupils, limb power, vitals) half-hourly for 2 hours, hourly for 12 hours, then 2-4 hourly to 24 hours; any deterioration routes to the deterioration danger-sign rule rather than the next routine check

title: Shunt and spina bifida lifelong follow-up enrolment
logic: VP shunt inserted or myelomeningocele closed AND no follow-up appointments (neurosurgical review plus, for spina bifida, urology/physiotherapy) booked at discharge
action: Block discharge checklist until 2-week and 3-month neurosurgical reviews are booked and, for spina bifida, the multidisciplinary referrals recorded; enrol caregiver in shunt-emergency education with documented understanding
